title: Yaman 6 Peanut (NSIC Pn 22): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: Yaman 6 Peanut: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: Yaman 6 peanut is a peanut variety. About 104 days to harvest, 1.8 t/ha in trials. See its ratings and traits. Compare it with others.
excerpt: Yaman 6 is a registered peanut variety, also sold or known as NSIC Pn 22 or Yaman peanut. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 2020 as NSIC 2020 Pn 22. It takes about 104 days from sowing to harvest, with 1.77 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for NSIC Pn 22 or Yaman peanut, this is the same peanut. Its seller and farm sources add notes, listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [peanut variety finder](/crop-varieties/peanut), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for legumes](/land-preparation/legume-land-preparation).

items: **Days to harvest:** about 104 days from sowing to harvest.
**Yield:** 1.77 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.
**Recommended for:** the areas in its trials, in the dry season.

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Yaman 6 peanut takes about 104 days from sowing to harvest. That is about the average of the 26 peanut varieties with a day count, 101.3 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 1.77 t/ha trails the average of its group, 1.85. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing. Its seller gives about 103 to 104 days.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in trials, rated under natural field conditions

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings on record. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain or pest population comes, so keep scouting.

The pests and diseases that hit peanut fields most often: [bacterial wilt](/diseases/bacterial-wilt), [eggplant leafhopper](/pests/eggplant-leafhopper), [bean fly](/pests/bean-fly), [Corn earworm](/pests/corn-earworm), [cutworm](/pests/cutworm). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
A hundred seeds weigh about 55.1 grams, so the higher this number, the bigger the seed. The seed holds 24.7 percent crude protein.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Yield:** 1.79 t/ha dry season, 1.74 t/ha wet season.
**Fruit:** About 55 g per 100 seeds, about 70 percent shelling.
**Where:** Dry season in Negros Occidental and North Cotabato.
Resistant to rust and Cercospora leaf spot.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: the newest peanut in the registry list, bred for dry season growing in Negros and North Cotabato. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Yaman 6 peanut
It is recommended for the dry season. Mani needs loose, well drained soil to fill its pods. Pick a variety by seed size for your buyer, and one rated against rust and leaf spot for the wet season.

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.

items.q: Is NSIC Pn 22 the same as Yaman 6?
items.a: Yes. NSIC Pn 22 is another name for Yaman 6, registered as NSIC 2020 Pn 22. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes about 104 days from sowing to harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 1.77 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Yaman 6?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
